statements.t: The Company now expects our Yeti and Yeti II plants to begin operations in the second quarter of 2027 and third quarter of 2027, earlier than previously expected.
Construction continues on our Roadrunner III, Copperhead II, Wrangler, Ranger, and Ranger II plants in the Permian Delaware, and these projects remain on track.
We are evaluating the timing and expect these new plants will likely be needed in 2028 or early 2029.

In our L&T segment, Targa recently commenced operations of our Train 12 fractionator in Mont Belvieu, TX and our Bull Run Extension intra-basin residue gas pipeline project in the fourth quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule.

Construction continues on our Train 13 fractionator, Speedway NGL Pipeline, GPMT LPG Export Expansion, and Buffalo Run, Bull Run II, and Forza intra-basin residue gas pipeline projects, which remain on track.
For the first quarter of 2027, management intends to recommend to Targa’s Board of Directors an increase to its common dividend to $1.50 per common share or $6.00 per common share annualized.
Beyond 2027, we expect to be in position to continue to provide meaningful annual increases to our common dividend.
We will host a conference call for the investment community at 11:00 a.m.

The Company defines adjusted free cash flow as adjusted cash flow from operations less maintenance capital expenditures and growth capital expenditures, net of any reimbursements of project costs and contributions from noncontrolling interests, and including contributions to investments in unconsolidated affiliates.

statements.t: In response to increasing production and to meet the infrastructure needs of producers and our downstream customers, our major expansion projects include the following:
In November 2026, we announced plans to construct a new 150 MBbl/d fractionation train in Mont Belvieu, Texas (“Train 14”).

In September 2025, we announced plans to construct the Speedway NGL Pipeline (“Speedway”) which will transport NGLs from our existing assets and future plant additions in the Permian Basin to our fractionation and storage complex in Mont Belvieu, Texas.
Our effective export capacity will increase up to 19 MMBbl per month, depending upon the mix of propane and butane demand, vessel size and availability of supply, among other factors.
We do not expect there to be any audit adjustments that would materially change our taxable income.

Our growing capital expenditures for pipelines and gathering and processing assets underpinned by fee-based margin, expansion of our Downstream facilities, continued focus on adding fee-based margin to our existing and future gathering and processing contracts, as well as third-party acquisitions of businesses and assets, will continue to increase the number of our contracts that are fee-based.

We define adjusted free cash flow as adjusted cash flow from operations less maintenance capital expenditures and growth capital expenditures, net of any reimbursements of project costs and contributions from noncontrolling interests, and including contributions to investments in unconsolidated affiliates.
